title: Ephemeral Key Wrap + Evidence Chronicle for KMS/HSM Integrations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Build a reliable orchestration layer that issues ephemeral wrapping keys to application components, coordinates customer/tenant key rotation with HSM-backed KEKs, and produces a tamper-evident 'evidence chronicle' (signed bundle) suitable for auditors. Scope includes an automated pipeline that correlates rotation events, residency assertions, and encryption metadata into a queryable, per-tenant artifact.

In-scope:
- Integration adapters for major cloud KMS providers and on-prem HSMs (wrap/unwrap, key metadata fetch, rotation hooks).
- Ephemeral wrap key issuance workflow for short-lived application envelopes to reduce exposure of tenant-wrapped data keys.
- Evidence chronicle format: JSONL signed bundles with event timestamps, key version digests, operator identity, and residency tags.
- Automation that emits chronicle artifacts into S3 (or customer-controlled storage) and indexes entries in an internal search sink for auditor access.
- Backwards-compatible fallbacks for tenants without HSM: record software-wrapped events with additional attestations.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end demo: create tenant key, perform rotation, issue ephemeral wrap key, encrypt/decrypt sample payload, and generate a chronicle bundle that verifies with an audit verifier tool.
2) Chronicle schema v1 documented in Confluence with field-level semantics and signature verification steps.
3) Automated tests covering rotation race conditions, wrap key expiry enforcement, and provenance metadata preservation.
4) Baseline performance: additional per-encrypt latency <= 12ms p95 when using ephemeral wrap path, and no increase in peak scheduler failures under load tests.
5) Delivery includes an operational runbook for failures, with clear steps to reconstitute evidence bundles and to re-run reconciliation for missed events.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes attached in links. Decided to lean on existing kms-adapter abstraction but add explicit ephemeral_wrap() call. Priority: deliver chronicle format and verifier first.

2025-01-22 - Diego Morales: Initial prototype of ephemeral wrap issuer in feature branch. Observed a race when concurrent rotations hit the same tenant KEK; added optimistic compare-and-swap for key-version binding.

2025-01-28 - Security Review (Priya Rao): Requested threat model update for ephemeral key leakage scenarios and a stronger signature scheme for chronicle bundles. Suggested using Ed25519 with key id rotation and keyset metadata in each bundle.

2025-02-04 - Diego Morales: Implemented chronicle signer service and added signature verification helper to the audit CLI. Pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1284. Marked tests flaky due to timing tolerances; investigating.
2025-02-10 - Design feedback (Samir Patel): Requested clearer residency tagging semantics for multi-region tenants. Agreed to add region_priority field and fallback regional statements in the schema.

2025-02-14 - QA (Maya Lopez): End-to-end smoke tests pass on staging. Found one edge case where HSM-side rotation notifications arrive out-of-order; added sequencing id and reconciliation job to detect and correct ordering issues.
Next steps: finish reconciliation job, complete integration tests for Azure HSM provider adapter, and land PR for chronicle generation + verifier.
